title: Radioactivity — 40 MCQs
description: Covers alpha, beta and gamma radiation, laws of radioactive disintegration, half-life, mean life and decay constant, Geiger-Müller tube, carbon dating, and medical uses and health hazards of nuclear radiation.

questions.q: Alpha particles are
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is a helium-4 nucleus consisting of two protons and two neutrons.

questions.q: Beta particles are
questions.explanation: Beta particles are electrons (β⁻) or positrons (β⁺) emitted from the nucleus.

questions.q: Gamma rays are
options: electromagnetic radiation of very short wavelength
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy photons emitted from excited nuclei.

questions.q: The penetrating power is greatest for
questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the highest penetrating power among the three common radiations.

questions.q: The ionizing power is greatest for
questions.explanation: Alpha particles, being heavy and doubly charged, produce the densest ionization.

questions.q: The decay constant λ is related to half-life T½ by
questions.explanation: T½ = ln 2 / λ ≈ 0.693 / λ, therefore λ = 0.693 / T½.

questions.q: The mean life τ of a radioactive sample is
questions.explanation: Mean life (average lifetime) τ = 1 / λ.

questions.q: The unit of activity is the
questions.explanation: One becquerel equals one disintegration per second.

questions.q: A Geiger-Müller tube is used to
questions.explanation: The GM tube detects ionizing radiation by the ionization of a gas and subsequent avalanche.

questions.q: Carbon dating is based on the radioactive isotope
questions.explanation: Radiocarbon dating uses the decay of ¹⁴C which is continuously produced in the atmosphere.

questions.q: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 10 days. After 30 days the fraction remaining is
questions.explanation: Three half-lives elapse: (1/2)³ = 1/8.

questions.q: A sample has a decay constant of 0.0693 day⁻¹. Its half-life is
The activity of a sample falls from 800 Bq to 100 Bq in 6 hours. The half-life is
questions.explanation: 800 → 400 → 200 → 100 requires three half-lives in 6 h, so T½ = 2 h.

questions.q: In alpha decay the mass number of the nucleus decreases by
questions.explanation: An α-particle carries away 4 nucleons, so A decreases by 4.

questions.q: In beta-minus decay the atomic number of the nucleus
questions.explanation: A neutron converts into a proton, increasing Z by 1 while A remains unchanged.

questions.q: The relation between half-life and mean life is
questions.explanation: T½ = ln 2 / λ = 0.693 τ since τ = 1/λ.

questions.q: A radioactive sample has an activity of 2 μCi. After two half-lives the activity becomes
questions.explanation: Activity halves with each half-life: 2 → 1 → 0.5 μCi.

questions.q: The probability of decay of a nucleus in a short time Δt is
questions.explanation: By definition the decay probability in time Δt is λ Δt.

questions.q: In a Geiger-Müller tube the gas is usually
options: a low-pressure inert gas with a quenching vapour
questions.explanation: GM tubes are filled with a noble gas plus a small amount of quenching gas at reduced pressure.

questions.q: The half-life of ¹⁴C is about 5730 years. The decay constant is approximately
A living organism has an activity of 15 decays per minute per gram of carbon. An archaeological sample shows 3.75 decays per minute per gram. The age of the sample is approximately
questions.explanation: Activity has fallen to 1/4, which corresponds to two half-lives: 2 × 5730 = 11460 years.

questions.q: Gamma rays are emitted from a nucleus when
options: it is in an excited state after α or β emission
an electron is captured from the K-shell only
the nucleus splits into two equal parts
questions.explanation: After α or β decay the daughter nucleus is often left in an excited state and de-excites by emitting γ-rays.

questions.q: The number of nuclei remaining after time t is given by
questions.explanation: The exponential decay law is N = N₀ exp(−λt).

questions.q: One curie is equal to
questions.explanation: 1 Ci = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ disintegrations per second = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq.

questions.q: Medical use of radioisotopes includes
options: only sterilization of instruments by α-particles
questions.explanation: Radioisotopes are widely used for both diagnostic imaging and therapeutic irradiation.

questions.q: A radioactive nuclide has a half-life of 5 hours. The fraction of the original sample left after 15 hours is
questions.explanation: 15 h = 3 half-lives; remaining fraction = (1/2)³ = 1/8.

questions.q: The activity of a sample is 8 × 10¹⁰ Bq. If the decay constant is 0.02 s⁻¹ the number of undecayed nuclei is
A sample initially contains 10²⁰ nuclei. Its half-life is 10 days. The number of nuclei left after 30 days is
questions.explanation: After 3 half-lives N = 10²⁰ / 8 = 1.25 × 10¹⁹.

questions.q: The mean life of a radioisotope is 10 years. Its half-life is approximately
In a GM counter the dead time is the time during which
options: the tube cannot register another count after a pulse
questions.explanation: After an avalanche the tube is insensitive for a short recovery (dead) time until the ions are cleared.

questions.q: An ancient wooden sample has a ¹⁴C activity of 3 counts per minute while a fresh sample has 12 counts per minute. Taking T½ = 5730 y the age of the sample is
questions.explanation: Activity ratio = 1/4 ⇒ two half-lives have elapsed ⇒ age = 2 × 5730 = 11460 y.

questions.q: The number of α-particles emitted per second by 1 g of pure ²²⁶Ra (T½ = 1600 y, N_A = 6.02 × 10²³) is approximately
A radioactive source has a half-life of 2 hours. The fraction of the original activity remaining after 6 hours is
questions.explanation: Six hours = three half-lives; remaining activity fraction = 1/8.

questions.q: The probability that a given nucleus will decay in the next one second is 10⁻⁶. The half-life of the nucleus is approximately
Health hazards of ionizing radiation include
options: damage to living cells and increased risk of cancer
only temporary heating of the body
questions.explanation: Ionizing radiation can break chemical bonds in DNA, leading to cell death or mutations and cancer risk.

questions.q: The activity of a radioactive sample is A₀ at t = 0. The activity at time t = 2/λ is
questions.explanation: A = A₀ e^{−λt} = A₀ e^{−λ·(2/λ)} = A₀ e⁻².

questions.q: In β⁺ decay a proton inside the nucleus is converted into
options: a neutron, a positron and a neutrino
questions.explanation: β⁺ decay: p → n + e⁺ + ν_e.

questions.q: A source has an initial activity of 1600 Bq and a half-life of 4 days. The activity after 12 days is
questions.explanation: 12 days = 3 half-lives; activity = 1600 / 8 = 200 Bq.

questions.q: The ratio of the number of nuclei left after time t to the initial number is e^{−λt}. The ratio of the number that have decayed to the initial number is
questions.explanation: Number decayed = N₀ − N = N₀(1 − e^{−λt}).

questions.q: For carbon dating to be accurate the assumption that must hold is that the
options: production rate of ¹⁴C in the atmosphere has been roughly constant
half-life of ¹⁴C changes with time
organism continues to exchange carbon after death
questions.explanation: The method relies on a known, approximately constant atmospheric ¹⁴C/¹²C ratio during the lifetime of the organism.
